alabama.fact: Montgomery was the first capital of the Confederacy and the home of the 1955 bus boycott.

alaska.fact: The biggest state by far, over twice the size of Texas; bought from Russia in 1867.

arizona.fact: Most of the state skips daylight saving time; the Navajo Nation inside it doesn't.

arkansas.fact: Home to the only public diamond mine where visitors keep what they find.

california.fact: The most populous state, with an economy bigger than most countries'.

colorado.fact: Admitted in the nation's 100th year; it has the highest average elevation of any state.

connecticut.fact: Its 1639 Fundamental Orders are often called the first written constitution.

delaware.fact: First to ratify the Constitution; most big US companies are incorporated here.

florida.fact: The longest coastline in the lower 48, and home of the Everglades.

georgia.fact: The largest state east of the Mississippi by land area.

hawaii.fact: The newest state, and the only one made up entirely of islands.

idaho.fact: Grows about a third of America's potatoes.

illinois.fact: The "Land of Lincoln" on its license plates; Lincoln is buried in Springfield.

indiana.fact: Home of the Indianapolis 500, the largest single-day sporting event in the world.

iowa.fact: Its caucuses have traditionally kicked off presidential primary season.

kansas.fact: The geographic center of the lower 48 is near Lebanon, Kansas.

kentucky.fact: Makes about 95% of the world's bourbon and hosts the Kentucky Derby.

louisiana.fact: Divided into parishes instead of counties, a holdover from French and Spanish rule.

maine.fact: The only state that borders just one other state (New Hampshire).

maryland.fact: Gave up land to create Washington, DC; "The Star-Spangled Banner" was written at Baltimore.

massachusetts.fact: The Pilgrims landed at Plymouth here in 1620; Harvard is the oldest US university.

michigan.fact: Two peninsulas, joined by the Mackinac Bridge, touching four of the five Great Lakes.

minnesota.fact: "Land of 10,000 Lakes" undersells it: it has nearly 12,000; the Mississippi starts here.

mississippi.fact: The birthplace of the blues, and of Elvis Presley (in Tupelo).

missouri.fact: Borders eight states, tied with Tennessee for the most; the Gateway Arch is in St. Louis.

montana.fact: The largest landlocked state; Glacier National Park is here.

nebraska.fact: The only state with a one-house (unicameral) legislature.

nevada.fact: The driest state; became a state mid-Civil War, hence "Battle Born" on its flag.

new-hampshire.fact: Holds the first presidential primary; its motto is "Live Free or Die."

new-mexico.fact: Santa Fe, founded around 1610, is the oldest state capital in the US.

new-york.fact: New York City was the first US capital, where Washington took office in 1789.

north-carolina.fact: The Wright brothers first flew at Kitty Hawk here in 1903.

north-dakota.fact: Admitted the same day as South Dakota; which came first was kept secret.

ohio.fact: Birthplace of seven presidents, and of astronauts John Glenn and Neil Armstrong.

oklahoma.fact: Formerly Indian Territory; about 39 tribal nations are headquartered here.

oregon.fact: Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the US; the Oregon Trail ended here.

pennsylvania.fact: The Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were both signed in Philadelphia.

rhode-island.fact: The smallest state, and the last of the original 13 to ratify the Constitution.

south-carolina.fact: The Civil War's first shots were fired at Fort Sumter, in Charleston harbor.

south-dakota.fact: Mount Rushmore and the Badlands are both here.

tennessee.fact: Home of country music in Nashville and blues and Graceland in Memphis.

texas.fact: An independent republic for nearly ten years before joining the US.

utah.fact: Five national parks, including Zion and Arches; the Great Salt Lake is saltier than the ocean.

vermont.fact: The top US maple syrup producer; Montpelier is the only state capital without a McDonald's.

virginia.fact: Birthplace of eight presidents, more than any other state; Jamestown was settled here in 1607.

washington.fact: The only state named after a president.

west-virginia.fact: Split from Virginia during the Civil War rather than join the Confederacy.

wisconsin.fact: "America's Dairyland" makes about a quarter of the country's cheese.

wyoming.fact: The least populous state, and the first to give women the vote (as a territory, in 1869).
